The $3$–free set $\{0,1\}^{k}\subset {\mathbf Z}_{3}^{k}$ has
$2^{k}$ elements in $3^{k}$ consecutive integers. For $3^{3}<32<3^{4}$
this gives $12$ e.g.

$$\{1,2,4,5,10,11,13,14,28,29,31,32\}$$

which is maximal for $n\le 32$.

$$12$$

The $k$ sums $a+b\;(a\le b)$ are $\tfrac{k(k+1)}2$ in
number and the $k(k-1)/2$ positive differences $a_{j}-a_{i}>0$
are distinct.  Hence

$$\frac{k(k-1)}2\le 25\qquad {\rm and}\qquad \frac{k(k+1)}2\le 51$$

so $k\le 7$.  The bound $7$ is attainable, e.g. the
Golomb ruler

$$\{1,2,5,11,19,24,26\}$$

has the $21$ positive differences

$$1,4,10,18,23,25,3,9,17,22,24,6,14,19,21,8,13,15,5,7,2$$

pairwise distinct, hence the $28$ sums $a+b$ are pairwise
distinct.

$$7$$

The $k$ sums $a+b\;(a\le b)$ are $\tfrac{k(k+1)}2$ in
number and lie in $[2,70]$ and the $k(k-1)/2$ positive
differences $a-b>0$ are distinct and lie in $[1,34]$.
Hence

$$\frac{k(k-1)}2\le 34\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad k\le 8$$

and $k=8$ is attainable, e.g.

$$\{1,2,5,10,16,23,33,35\}$$

has $28$ distinct positive differences and $36$ distinct
sums.

$$8$$

With $k=|S|$ the $\binom{k}{2}$ differences
$|a-b|>0$ are distinct and

$${\binom{k}{2}}\le 44\qquad {\rm i.e.}\qquad k\le 9$$

and $k=9$ is attainable.  In particular
${\binom{k+1}{2}}\le 89$ gives the trivial $k\le 12$.
